name: Raymond Realty Ltd
title: Raymond Realty Ltd - 544420 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Pre-sales-led growth with JDA mix now 54% of FY26 bookings and FY26 EBITDA margin ~16%, guided 16-18% for FY27; management expects cash-negative operations for two years and Thane pre-sales flat at INR1,300-1,500 crore.

summary.headline: Raymond Realty FY26 total income rose 29% to INR3,039 crores; Q4 income up 53% to INR1,176 crores with 139% YoY bookings surge.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of validation, with total income of INR3,039 crores (+29% YoY), Q4 income of INR1,176 crores (+53%) and FY26 blended EBITDA of INR495 crores at roughly 16% margin, versus 13% in the first nine months. Q4 EBITDA margin was 21.5% as stated in the opening remarks and about 21% per the Q&A. JDA share of pre-sales reached 54% in FY26, a 50:50 own-land-to-JDA mix target achieved a year ahead of FY27 schedule. Management guided FY27 blended EBITDA margin of 16% to 18%, minimum 20% growth in pre-sales and top-line, and cash-negative operations for the next two years.

financial_highlights.change: vs around 13% in first nine months

financial_highlights.value: 139% YoY surge (quarter as stated, not specified)

segments.name: Thane (own legacy land, Pokhran Road)
segments.commentary: Pokhran Road 100-acre land has total revenue potential of INR25,000 crores, with about 60 acres under development. Thane pre-sales were INR1,360 crores in FY26 versus INR1,800 crores in FY25 and INR1,950 crores in FY24; management says the 4-5 year average of INR1,300-1,500 crores is achievable. Pokhran Road pre-sales were close to INR1,400 crores in FY27 to date.

segments.name: JDA portfolio (non-Thane)
segments.commentary: Seven JDA projects with combined revenue potential of about INR17,000 crores, including Kandivali (GDV INR3,000 crores, 70% revenue share to Raymond). JDAs were 22% of booking values in FY25 and 54% of pre-sales in FY26 from non-Thane land.

segments.name: Q4 launches
segments.commentary: Address by GS Wadala and Address by GS Sion together released combined GDV of almost INR6,400 crores. Sion launched on 24 March 2026, so had only about one week of selling; Park Street (retail, Thane) and TenX District 9 were also launched in Thane.

segments.name: TenX Habitat (Thane)
segments.commentary: First project launched by the company, about 3,100 homes, fully sold out and has received full OC during the year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 blended EBITDA margin guided at 16% to 18%, range-bound, versus about 16% in FY26.
Minimum 20% growth in pre-sales and top-line guided; management said FY27 will do better than that.
Two more Mahim projects expected to launch by Q3 FY27; Kandivali to spill over into FY28.
Next two years expected to be cash negative on an overall basis; internal accruals of INR600-650 crores (Thane INR450-500 crores plus JDA INR100-150 crores) to keep growing.
Construction cost impact of 3-4% possible if commodity pressure persists for a long period; management expects to pass it on and sees no EBITDA impact.
Debt-to-equity to stay below internal 1:1 ceiling; liquidity buffer said to fully fund next year's requirements.
Target to reach 20% EBITDA margin on each JDA as quickly as possible; FY27 seen as good, FY28 even better.
capex_capacity: Two Mahim projects in advanced approvals, to launch by Q3 FY27; Kandivali to follow, spilling into FY28.
Company is asset-light: JDAs signed without land purchase, but approval costs paid to government are substantial and weigh on cash flow.
Thane has a master-planned commercial area earmarked (not announced); management said activation timing is not far but no decision yet.
Thane inventory sufficient for next six months; two more Thane launches planned during FY27.
JDA time to launch varies: average 15-18 months, from 6-7 months (Wadala) to about 2.5 years (Mahim).
demand_pricing: Thane competition described as intense for 20 years; limited price growth, so volume is main growth lever. Thane pricing ranges INR7,000 to INR25,000 per sq ft; Pokhran Road is INR23,000-25,000.
Bandra first JDA (Address by GS): earlier guidance about INR2,100 crores revenue; management expects to beat it on top-line.
Management said some Mumbai redevelopment markets are overheated; JDA pipeline deals spilled into FY27.
Business development pipeline: FY26 added about INR3,000 crores of GDV against an earlier 5,000-10,000 crore guidance (per analyst).
Focus on Western Suburbs and BKC; South Bombay only if deal structure and returns make sense.
Pre-sales seasonality: Q1 and Q2 light, Q3 and Q4 stronger.
Revenue recognised on percentage-of-completion basis; management said no lumpiness.
Pre-sales collections are construction-linked; about 80% collected by superstructure completion in a 4-year project.

qa_highlights.question: Thane pre-sales have fallen from INR1,950 crores (FY24) to INR1,360 crores (FY26). Is competition rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Thane sales depend on each year's product mix; competition has been intense for 20 years. Average Thane sales of INR1,300-1,500 crores a year are achievable; no cause for concern.

qa_highlights.question: Why do JDA launch timelines vary so much (e.g., Mahim signed in CY23 still not launched)?
qa_highlights.answer: Each deal differs by maturity and counterparty speed. BKC took about 9 months from start; Mahim has taken about 2.5 years due to society governance issues. Average is 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook and how is it booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended FY26 margin about 16%; new JDAs start in single digits but are contracted at 20%+. FY27 blended margin guided at 16-18%. Revenue recognised on percentage-of-completion basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective economic interest in Kandivali and Sion sales response?
qa_highlights.answer: Kandivali GDV INR3,000 crores with 70% revenue share to Raymond, target margin about 20-22%. Pokhran Road pre-sales around INR1,400 crores in FY27 so far; Sion launched 24 March (about one week of selling) with strong response.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No: management expects cash-negative operations for the next two years; internal accruals of INR600-650 crores to keep growing and be reinvested.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of commodity and Morbi gas-supply disruption on costs?
qa_highlights.answer: 3-4% cost impact possible if prolonged; no material impact if resolved in 2-3 months. Suppliers continue at contracted rates; no supply disruption; management sees no EBITDA impact.

risks_watch: Thane pre-sales have declined for two years (INR1,950 crores FY24, INR1,800 crores FY25, INR1,360 crores FY26) and depend on product mix and limited pricing power.
JDA launch timing is uncertain: partner governance (e.g., Mahim) can extend time to launch by 2+ years.
Negative operating cash flow expected for two years; approval costs are substantial; around INR4,000 crores pending collections to watch.
Input cost inflation of 3-4% if commodity and gas-supply constraints persist for a long period.
Business development slower in some overheated redevelopment markets; deals spilling into FY27.
Valuation remains low; management said market awaits consistency over 6-8 quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 delivery and margins, but defensive on Thane sales decline and stock valuation; management repeatedly asked investors for patience. Some figures were corrected on the call (Sion launch duration and Q4 margin references), and there were minor inconsistencies on the Thane GDV and Q4 margin figures.
key_quotes: So, whatever we had planned for, we feel validated on all of those numbers.
we don't sign any JDA which will give us less than 20% EBITDA margin.
So the short answer to your question is going forward for the next two years, we will be cash negative on an overall basis but internal accruals will keep on growing
You will not see lumpiness in our reporting which is the case with some of the other players because a lot of them follow completed contract methods.

Kandivali JDA (GDV INR3,000 crores, 70% revenue share) to spill over into FY28

growth.why: Management guides minimum 20% growth in pre-sales and top-line for FY27 (management says it will do better), backed partly by Q4 launches (Address by GS Wadala and Sion, ~INR6,400 crores GDV), two Mahim projects by Q3 FY27 and two Thane launches in FY27, but no hard capacity build-out; Thane volume held at INR1,300-1,500 crores a year.
